masseng_boundary.note: tutoring/learning production is NOT implemented in MASSENG v5; synthetic demonstration only. Bray targets are literature targets, not a fit.

label: SIMULATION - stipulated tutoring demand + production DGP; no causal claim

single_process.tobit_scale: log1p(T): same units as the 0.8 semi-elasticity truth; the estimate is NOT close to 0.8 (see tobit_within_0.15_share); level-scale fit reported separately and never compared to 0.8

different_processes.tobit_scale: log1p(T): same units as the 0.8 semi-elasticity truth; the estimate is NOT close to 0.8 (see tobit_within_0.15_share); level-scale fit reported separately and never compared to 0.8

gini_domain: exp(learning index) - strictly positive level domain; the raw additive achievement index is non-positive in ~37% of draws, where the Gini is undefined
plain_result: Tutoring behaves as one exams-shadow module for demand: on the log1p scale (same units as the 0.8 truth) the two-part model is closer than the Tobit (0.73 vs 1.37). The log1p Tobit does NOT recover the truth, so the dropped pre-registered single-process rule fails (Tobit within-0.15 share 0.00). On inequality the own-teacher ban does NOT raise the learning Gini once the Gini is computed on a strictly positive level domain: in this reduced production model there is no substitution margin, so removing tutoring lowers the Gini in every CES/retention specification (delta range -0.064..-0.041). The illustrative model is far from Bray's targets (max |z| = 10.6), so nothing here is a fit to a real shadow-education system.

statistical_frame.scale_alignment: Tobit on log1p(T) so its income coefficient is in the same UNITS as the 0.8 semi-elasticity truth; it does NOT recover 0.8 (1.441 single / 1.370 different, 0.64/0.57 away), and the level-scale Tobit is reported but never compared to 0.8
